issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() to return a double, but the solution implementation defines getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() to return an int. The template contains a TODO for implementing this method (no signature), which may lead students to follow the UML (double) while the reference solution and likely tests use an int. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected return type and whether to perform floating-point division or integer division.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the UML and problem text to specify an int return type for getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(), or (B) change the solution (and mention in the template) so getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() returns a double and performs floating-point division (e.g. return (double) getTotalNumberOfStudents() / getNumberOfTutors();). Ensure the chosen type is reflected in the UML, template comments, and solution/tests.
